SUMMARY

I worked on brand project management, multichannel e-commerce operations and creator partnerships for a small Irish wellness brand with no large marketing budget. This portfolio shows the systems I used to run TikTok Shop, Shopify and Amazon and keep a small team on track, then how I find and track creators, what happened when one of them broke out, and the videos and graphics I worked on. Where the work was a team effort, each entry says what I did. The screenshots show the stores, invitation waves, sample shipping and sales data behind the results.

PART 1 · BRAND PROJECT MANAGEMENT & MULTICHANNEL E-COMMERCE OPERATIONS
1 · OPERATIONS & PROCESS

One tracked system for strategy, outreach, operations and content

Task: Replace scattered WhatsApp coordination with one place for tasks, deadlines and goals across Shopify, Amazon UK/Ireland and TikTok Shop.

My role: Built and ran four Asana projects (brand strategy and goals, TikTok Shop affiliate strategy, multi-channel operations and a content calendar), wrote SOPs, and set up a weekly team check-in rhythm.

Tools: Asana, Google Workspace.

Result: SOPs for content production and affiliate management, documented team roles, quarterly goals (including affiliate creator count and posting cadence), and weekly cross-channel reporting.

2 · MULTICHANNEL E-COMMERCE OPERATIONS

Running the Shopify store

Task: Run the Shopify store as the brand’s own channel: convert visitors, capture emails and keep the store consistent with Amazon and TikTok Shop.

My role: Worked on the Shopify store day to day with the founder, designers and developers: weekly performance checks, email capture and welcome-offer set-up, and coordinating content and design changes.

Tools: Shopify, GA4, Asana.

Result: A live storefront with social proof on the home page (4.4 stars, 400+ reviews), a product page with pack-size pricing and a shipping promise, TikTok videos embedded on the page, and a welcome offer of 20% off with free shipping on a first order. The operations board tracked a weekly Shopify performance check and the email capture set-up, both completed.

Amazon UK and Ireland

Task: Keep the brand’s Amazon UK and Ireland listing converting and collecting reviews.

My role: Planned and tracked the Amazon UK/Ireland workstream on the operations board, including the listing title and bullets and a review-generation process.

Tools: Asana (Amazon UK Operations board).

Result: Both tasks are marked complete on the board. The brand’s Shopify home page and TikTok profile cite its #1 Best Seller position on Amazon Ireland, the channel these tasks supported.

TikTok Shop

Running the TikTok Shop Seller Centre

Task: Keep the TikTok Shop side of the business running day to day: orders, returns and payouts.

My role: Managed Seller Centre administration alongside the other channels, including shipping orders, return settings and checking weekly payouts.

Tools: TikTok Shop Seller Centre.

Result: Over the months the shop was operating (17 March to 14 September 2026), TikTok Shop Ireland recorded GMV of €2,015.08 from 107 orders, 106 customers and 133 items sold. Returns, payouts and order queues were handled in one place. On 9 June the standard return shipping rebate was 50% with a 0.0% return and refund rate shown, and the week of 8 to 14 June paid out €101.51 with €72 on hold. Payouts arrive every Monday.

PART 2 · CREATOR & INFLUENCER PARTNERSHIPS
3 · CREATOR RESEARCH & OUTREACH

Finding creators, shipping product and tracking every contact

Task: Find creators who fit a functional wellness brand, approach them, send gifted product, and track each one from first contact to posted content.

My role: Researched creators on Instagram and TikTok, contacted and followed up with them, arranged product shipments, and kept the creator tracker up to date.

Tools: Reacher, Kalodata, a creator tracker spreadsheet, TikTok Shop affiliate tools, Asana.

Result: 47 creators logged, 37 contacted and 37 sent gifted product. The tracker followed each one through outreach, shipping, delivery, content due date, post link and follow-up. This process produced the 190K-view video in section 4.

Reaching Irish creators at scale through TikTok Shop

Task: Reach more creators than one-to-one outreach allows, using TikTok Shop’s own invitation tools, and make it easy for them to say yes.

My role: Set up target collaboration invitations to Irish creators, each with a short pitch and the product attached, set commission rates, and tracked who accepted.

Tools: TikTok Shop Affiliate Centre (target and open collaboration), Asana.

Result: Two Ireland waves were live on 10 August 2026. Wave 1 invited 22 creators and 2 accepted. Wave 3 invited 198 and 16 accepted. Acceptance was about 8% to 9% in both, so the wider list brought in roughly eight times as many creators. Five earlier invitations are marked completed.

Open collaboration: the LiquidCalm listings carry standard commissions of 15%, 20% and 30%, with Shop Ads commissions of 7% and 18% on two of them.

Getting product to creators who said yes

Task: Turn creators who said yes into posted content by getting samples out quickly.

My role: Reviewed incoming sample requests and processed free-sample orders for shipping in Seller Centre.

Tools: TikTok Shop Seller Centre and Affiliate Centre.

Result: On 10 August 2026, 11 sample orders were ready to ship, each with a platform ship-by deadline, and 1 request was waiting for review.

4 · CASE STUDY: CREATOR-LED GROWTH, MEASURED

How one creator video changed the shop’s numbers

Task: Find out which creator content works, with no paid budget, and measure what it does for the shop.

My role: Sourced and briefed the creator, reviewed the results in TikTok Business Suite, and wrote up what it meant for the founder.

Tools: TikTok Business Suite, Kalodata.

Result: A single video reached 190K views, 796 likes, 25 comments and 103 shares, and about 71% of the shop’s year-to-date TikTok views fell in the 28 days around it.

On 26 August 2026, four videos from the same campaign went live on the same day. Three reached 1.3K, 2.3K and 0 views as tests. The fourth reached 190K views, 796 likes, 25 comments and 103 shares, by far the strongest result in the set. What stood out was not a scripted pitch: the creator was easy to watch, and the content felt authentic rather than promotional. That is a useful signal for choosing creators, because fit and delivery matter as much as follower count.

Over the 28 days to 12 September, the shop reached 204,827 video views and 198,332 reached audience, concentrated around 26–28 August. Profile views rose by 396 in the same period.

The year-to-date view shows a long quiet baseline from January to July and then a sharp spike in late August. Growth came in concentrated bursts tied to specific creator content, so the next step I would take is a repeatable process: test several creators cheaply, back the ones who show real signal, and write down what worked.

What it did to the shop’s sales

Task: Check whether creator-led views turned into sales, not just attention.

My role: Pulled the Seller Centre and Affiliate Centre numbers from before and after the breakout and compared them.

Tools: TikTok Shop Seller Centre (dashboard and Shop analytics), Affiliate Centre performance.

Result: In the seven days to 26 August 2026 the shop recorded GMV of €580.45 from 31 orders and 30 customers, with 1,180 visitors. Every metric was sharply up on the previous period, and GMV was up about 720%. For comparison, Shop analytics shows €588.44 of GMV from 32 orders across 1 March to 10 August, so one week came close to matching the previous five months. Across the full operating period (17 March to 14 September) GMV reached €2,015.08 from 107 orders, which means about 70% of it came after 10 August.

Before the breakout, 20 creator videos in the 28 days to 8 June produced €83.75 of creator-attributed GMV from 5 items sold, and no LIVE streams. That is the baseline the August result should be read against.

Note: the first two figures come from two different Seller Centre views (the European dashboard for the seven days to 26 August, and Shop analytics for Ireland from 1 March to 10 August), so treat the comparison as indicative. The 70% share is my own calculation from two Shop analytics views with slightly different start dates (1 March and 17 March).

What I took from it: twenty videos in four weeks moved little, while one video from a creator who fit moved far more. That supports choosing creators for fit over volume.

APPROACH

Everything above is small-scale, resource-constrained work, and it is the discipline I bring to creator partnerships: find the cheapest, fastest signal first, look closely at what is actually working before scaling it, and build repeatable process around what proves out, while being honest about what is a proven win and what is still in progress.
